title: Calradia Remembers: a written tale
description: GENERATED from CalradiaRemembers.Logic.AuthoredQuests by the Maps suite (QuestSchemaMap). Do not edit: regenerate with Tools/Update-Maps.ps1. A file holds one tale, or a list of tales.

AuthoredQuest.description: One authored quest, as its file describes it.

id.description: Unique across every file. Prefix it with your mod's name.

author.description: Who wrote it. Shown to nobody in game; for the reader of the file.

unique.description: On (the default): played once per campaign, won or lost. Off: it may come back.

repeat_cooldown_days.description: For a tale that is not unique: how many days after it ended before it may be offered again.

weight.description: When a character could give several tales, they are chosen in proportion to their weights. 0 is never offered. Default 10.

requires.description: Who may give the tale, and what it needs of the world and of the player.

on_map.description: The tale begins by itself on the map, never in a conversation: when the player's party has stood still long enough, by day, in the giver's own lands, on a chance each day. The giver must travel with the player (requires.giver.with_player).

on_scenario.description: The tale is opened only by a scenario rule (OPEN_TALE), never offered in a conversation nor begun on the map: the rule names the giver. With an invitation, a popup asks the player first; without, the tale begins at once (its second stage, a scene in the chat, can ask in role-play instead). A stage that is a conversation with someone opens by itself.

binds.description: Every role your text uses, with a short description for the reader of the file. Each {role} is filled with a real name.

stages.description: The steps of the story, the first being the request itself.

reward.description: The single success ending: what the tale leaves when a path leads to "reward".

endings.description: Named endings, each with its own regard, gold, memory and consequences. A path leads to one with "end:<id>".

failure.description: What the tale leaves when its time runs out (days) before any ending is reached.

AuthoredRequires.description: When the quest may be offered, and by whom (increment 1: the shape the werewolf needs).

giver.description: The character who gives the tale.

village.description: The village the tale happens in, bound as {village}.

rival.description: A second lord the tale needs, bound as {rival}: the leader of another house of the giver's realm.

husband.description: The giver's husband, bound as {husband}. Needs requires.giver.married.

content.description: The content level the tale needs, as the mod options name it: none (every player), mature, explicit or hardcore. A tale is offered only when the player's setting reaches it.

AuthoredMapTrigger.description: How a tale that begins on the map is set off, and the popup that asks the player (Gabriel, 10/10/2026).

still_hours.description: Hours the player's party must have stood in the same place, out in the open. Default 3.

in_givers_lands.description: On (the default): only when the nearest settlement is of the giver's own culture.

chance_per_day.description: The chance the tale begins, once a day when everything else holds: above 0, at most 1. Default 0.15.

invitation.description: The popup's text, which sets the scene; {giver} is filled with the giver's name.

accept.description: The popup's yes, which begins the tale and opens the conversation with the giver.

decline.description: The popup's no: nothing is lost, and the tale may come back after a season.

AuthoredScenarioTrigger.description: The popup a scenario-opened tale shows (OPEN_TALE; Gabriel, 24/10/2026).

invitation.description: The popup's text, which sets the scene; {giver} is filled with the giver's name. Empty: no popup, the tale begins at once.

accept.description: The popup's yes, which begins the tale and opens the conversation with the giver.

decline.description: The popup's no: nothing is lost, and the tale may come back after a season.

decline_ending.description: An ending of "endings" the popup's no leads to: the tale is played to that ending at once (its memory, regard and consequences, its cooldown), instead of passing for a season. Needs an invitation.

AuthoredStage.description: One stage: a journal line, one verified objective, what the people involved know, and what follows.

id.description: The stage's name, used by "next" to lead here. Unique in the tale.

journal.description: The line logged in the quest journal when the stage begins.

image.description: An image file of the tale's own folder (.png or .jpg), or a video (.crvid, whose first frame is its picture), opened beside the chat when this stage's scene opens, or a conversation of this stage (with its characters or the people of its place).

image_pool.description: Several pictures or videos for this stage: each time the tale is played, one the player has not seen yet is chosen (all seen, they start over), and it holds for the whole tale. It stands in for "image".

image_pool_pick.description: How the image_pool picks: "unseen" (the default) one not seen yet, starting over once all were; "random" any of them each time, a repeat included.

objective.description: What the game checks to complete the stage. A stage with choices may have none.

canvas.description: How the moment feels. Spoken by the giver, when this stage is theirs to say. A line may hold only under a flag.

facts.description: What the giver must convey, without changing it. A fact may hold only under a flag.

knowers.description: Lines for other characters, framed as what they believe at this stage. The key is a role ("{giver}") or "locals_of:{place}".

choices.description: Ways out of this stage: by an act, by the player's choice in a scene, or by words in a conversation. The first taken wins.

on_complete.description: What follows when the stage's own objective is met.

on_enter.description: Consequences carried out when the tale enters this stage (the same kinds as an ending's, each with its own "if"), so a tale can carry someone away midway and bring them back later. Never on the first stage, which is the request.

AuthoredOutcome.description: What success, failure or a named ending leaves behind.

days.description: failure: the tale fails that many days after it was accepted.

regard.description: Added to the giver's regard for the player (negative takes it away).

gold.description: Paid to the player by the game; negative, the player pays it (a fine, a bribe, a child's keep) to the giver. A choice leading straight to an ending the player must pay for is offered only while the player has that much.

memory.description: What the giver remembers, in the giver's own voice.

journal.description: The last line written in the journal when the tale ends this way.

consequences.description: What else the ending leaves in the world. A consequence may hold only under a flag.

role.description: lord, notable, gang_leader, spouse (the player's own husband or wife), companion (one of the player's companions), or any.

holds.description: "{village}": the village is picked among the giver's clan villages. Without it, the giver's home settlement is used, when it is a village.

min_regard.description: The giver's regard for the player on Calradia Remembers' own ledger (the one built in conversation, not the game's relation).

not_at_war_with_player.description: On by default: a giver whose realm is at war with the player never offers it.

culture.description: The giver's culture, one or a list ("battania", or ["battania", "sturgia"]); empty for any.

realm.description: The giver's realm, one or a list, by its id or name ("vlandia", or ["empire", "empire_w"]); empty for any.

gender.description: female or male: the giver must be a woman, or a man; empty for either.

with_player.description: On: the giver must be travelling in the player's own party.

not_pregnant.description: On: never while the giver is with child.

married.description: On: the giver must be married, to someone other than the player (a tale that binds her husband needs it).

not_clan_leader.description: On: never a giver who leads her house (she could not leave it).

not_of_players_realm.description: On: never a giver of the player's own realm.

trade.description: A notable's trade, one or a list ("merchant", or ["merchant", "artisan"]): merchant, artisan, ruralnotable, headman, preacher. Only a notable has one; empty for any.

type.description: village, or town (a town is still named {village} in the tale's lines and roles).

near.description: "forest", or leave it empty for anywhere.

culture.description: The village's culture, one or a list ("battania", or ["battania", "sturgia"]); empty for any.

RivalRequirement.description: The {rival}: a clan leader of the giver's realm who is not the giver (branching tales, 04/10/2026).

role.description: clan_leader: the leader of another house of the giver's realm.

same_realm_as.description: "{giver}": the rival serves the same realm as the giver.

HusbandRequirement.description: The giver's husband, bound as {husband} (the Troy-inspired tale, Gabriel 12/10/2026).

role.description: spouse_of_giver: the giver's own husband or wife.

rules_a_realm.description: On: the husband must rule a realm (he declares its wars himself). Off: any husband, who presses his ruler.

gender.description: female or male: the tale is offered only to a woman, or a man; empty for either.

AuthoredObjective.description: One condition the engine verifies; which fields matter depends on Type.

hero.description: talk_to: the character, as a role ("{giver}"). war_ends, dies, weds_player: the person the world is watched for.

when.description: talk_to: "opened" (the default) completes the stage as the conversation opens; "closed" when it ends, so the whole conversation belongs to the stage and its ending sees what came of it.

count.description: talk_to_locals: how many different notables of the place. bring: how many of the goods (1 to 200).

radius.description: be_at, keep_watch: how near the place the party must be (default 5).

nights.description: keep_watch: [first night it may happen, night it surely happens].

chance.description: keep_watch: the chance each night from the first opens the scene (0 to 1).

days.description: wait: how many days must pass with no other choice taken.

scene.description: explore: the scene played in the chat.

spawn.description: defeat_party: the band spawned near the place.

item.description: bring: the goods asked, as the game names them: a kind (horses, livestock, grain), an item category (wine, iron, tools) or one item's id.

to.description: bring: who the goods are handed to, a role ({giver} when empty).

AuthoredChoice.description: One way out of a stage (branching tales, 04/10/2026).

id.description: The choice's name, unique in its stage.

label.description: What the player can do, in plain words. In a scene, it is listed under the narration and the narrator is told it.

journal.description: A line added to the journal under the stage's own, while this choice is open.

next.description: Where this choice leads: a stage id, "reward", or "end:<id>".

if.description: Flags that must hold for this choice to be open ("name", or "!name" for not set). A closed choice is never shown nor taken.

sets.description: Flags set when this choice is taken.

default.description: In a scene: taken when the scene closes with no choice made, if the stage has no on_complete.next.

objective.description: By an act: what the game checks (talk_to, return, talk_to_locals, be_at, defeat_party, wait). The first met wins.

said.description: By words: taken when, in a conversation with that character, the player says or agrees to what it means.

canvas.description: How the moment feels, for the character in whose conversation this choice is taken (as a stage's canvas).

facts.description: What that character must convey when this choice is taken.

knowers.description: Lines for that character, in the conversation that took this choice.

next.description: The next stage's id, "reward" to end the tale in success, or "end:<id>" for a named ending.

type.description: memory, world_event, grudge, conception, elope (she leaves her husband with the player), return_spouse (she goes back to him), item (the player is given an item) or regard (someone's regard for the player moves by amount).

who.description: memory: who remembers, a role or "locals_of:{place}". grudge: who holds it, a role. conception: the player's partner, a role ({giver} when empty). elope, return_spouse: the lady who leaves or goes back ({giver} when empty). regard: whose regard moves, a role ({giver} when empty).

text.description: memory: what they remember. grudge: the cause, in the holder's words.

summary.description: world_event: the news that spreads through the realm.

magnitude.description: world_event: how loud the news is, 0 to 100. grudge: how deep it runs, 0 to 100.

place.description: world_event: where it happened, as a role.

against.description: grudge: who it is held against, a role (Gabriel, 06/10/2026: a tale may set two lords at odds).

spouse.description: elope: the husband she leaves; return_spouse: the husband she goes back to. A role, {husband} when empty.

chance.description: conception: the chance of a child, 0 to 1; the game's own 0.15 when left out. The woman of the two carries it; two women or two men conceive nothing.

item.description: item: the item given to the player, by its id in the game ("wine", "sumpter_horse").

count.description: item: how many are given (1 to 200).

amount.description: regard: how far their regard for the player moves (negative lowers it), -100 to 100, never 0.

if.description: Flags that must hold for this consequence to be carried out.

AuthoredScene.description: An exploration scene: the chat with a narrator and no character, until someone is met.

title.description: The name over the chat window during the scene ("The burned barns of {village}"). Empty: "The wood by <village>".

opening.description: What the narrator opens the scene with.

findings.description: What there is to discover. Without choices, at least one must be required.

hazards.description: What the player's choices can spring. Each springs once.

encounters.description: People who may be met in the scene, voiced by the narrator.

closing.description: Shown when the scene closes, after any missed findings.

invite_prisoners.description: Off by default: the player's prisoners may be invited into this scene only when it is on (an interrogation in the wood).

AuthoredSpawn.description: A party spawned for the quest: real, on the map, beaten in a real battle.

id.description: The band's name in the file.

template.description: The bandit faction whose troops it is made of (looters by default), or "local": the bandits of the nearest hideout, a share of them seasoned as the player's men are.

near.description: The place it patrols around, as a role.

behavior.description: Read but not played yet (every band patrols around its place).

flee_after_days.description: The tale fails if the band is still alive that many days after the stage began.

scale_with_player.description: The band grows with the player's men (never below its size, up to a ceiling), so a climax stays one for a lord with an army.

on_defeat.description: What the tale makes of the player losing a fight to this band. Without it, a lost fight changes nothing: the player may try again until the tale's clocks run out.

AuthoredSaid.description: A choice taken by words: what the player must say, and to whom.

to.description: The character it must be said to, as a role: "{giver}" or "{rival}".

meaning.description: What the player's words must mean, plainly: "the player promises to keep silent for a price".

canvas.description: The scene as the player comes upon it.

facts.description: What must be true in the narration.

id.description: The finding's name, used in its marker.

image.description: An image file of the tale's own folder (.png or .jpg), or a video (.crvid, whose first frame is its picture), shown beside the chat when the narration reveals it.

required.description: A required finding the player never reached is told when the scene closes.

sets.description: Flags set when it is found (or told at closing).

id.description: The hazard's name, used in its marker.

image.description: An image file of the tale's own folder (.png or .jpg), or a video (.crvid, whose first frame is its picture), shown beside the chat when it springs.

trigger.description: What the player must do to spring it.

effect.description: What the game does when it springs.

id.description: The person's name in the file, used in its marker.

image.description: An image file of the tale's own folder (.png or .jpg), or a video (.crvid, whose first frame is its picture), shown beside the chat when they are met.

name.description: How the narrator names them ("a girl from {village}").

persona.description: Who they are and how they seem.

knows.description: What they know, and say only that.

sets.description: Flags set when they are met.

AuthoredDefeat.description: A lost fight against a tale's band (Gabriel, 10/10/2026): an ending of its own, or, without a next, the tale goes on (told once per stage: memories, news, a journal line), the band still there to beat before it flees.

next.description: An ending ("end:<id>") the tale reaches when the player loses to this band. Without it, the tale goes on.

regard.description: Added to the giver's regard for the player (negative takes it away).

memory.description: What the giver remembers of the defeat, in the giver's own voice.

journal.description: The line written in the journal when the player loses to this band.

consequences.description: What else the defeat leaves in the world (memory, world_event, grudge). A consequence may hold only under a flag.

hit_points.description: injure: [fewest, most] hit points taken, never below 1 HP.

party.description: alert: read but not played yet (every alert warns the stage's band).

hours.description: lose_time: read but not played yet (the scene ends, the night is lost).

line.description: A line, written plain, or under flags so it is said only while they hold.

if.description: Flags that must hold for the line to be said ("name", or "!name" for not set).

lines.description: One line, or a list of lines, each said while its flags hold.

flags.description: A flag's name ("name", or "!name" for not set), or a list of them; all must hold.
